INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR NANKING SAFETY ZONE
5 Ninghai Road

December 17th, 1937

The Imperial Japanese Embassy,
Nanking.

For the kind attention of
Mr Kiyoshi Fukui
Second Secretary to the Japanese Embassy.

Dear Sirs:

In view of the statement of Consul General Katsuo
Okazaki yesterday afternoon that the International Committee
had no legal status some explanations of our position seem to
be in order. Vis-a-vis your Japanese authorities we are not
claiming any political status whatever. But on December 1st
Mayor Ma of the Nanking Municipality turned over to our Committee
nearly all the functions of the City Government for the emergency
of transition police, supervision of essential utilities, fire
department, housing regulation, food supply and sanitation.
Consequently when your Army victoriously arrived in the city
on Monday noon, December 13th we were the only administrative
authority carrying on in the city. Of course that authority did
not extend outside of the Safety Zone itself and involved no
rights of sovereignty within the Zone.

Being the only administrative authorities and having
had assurances from the Japanese authorities in Shanghai that if
the Safety Zone did not contain soldiers or military establish-
ments your troops would not intentionally attack it we tried to
establish contact with your advance guard immediately. In the
afternoon of December 13th, we found a captain with a group of
Japanese soldiers resting on Han Chung Lu. We explained to him
where the Zone was and marked it on his map. We politely called
his attention to the three Red Cross Hospitals and told him about
the disarmed soldiers. He was reassuring so we felt that all was
understood by your Army.

That night and early the next morning we drew up our
letter of December 14th and had it translated into Japanese.
Then, as Mr. Fukuda, Attache to the Imperial Japanese Embassy, may
tell you, Mr. Rabe, Mr. Smythe, and Rev. Forster went to find a
high Japanese officer to whom we would present the letter. We
talked to five different officers but they told us to wait for the
arrival of the High Commander the next day.

The following morning, December 15th, we were favoured
by calls by Mr. Tokuyasu Fukuda of the Imperial Japanese Embassy,
and by Mr. Sekiguchi with cards from the Captain and Officers of the
H.I.J.M.S. Seto at our headquarters. We presented our letter of
December 14th, referred to above, to Mr. Fukuda and assured Mr.
Sekiguchi that we would be glad to cooperate in starting the elec-
tricity works. At noon, we had the pleasure of meeting the Head
of the T'ien Pei Kuan Chang at the Bank of Communications and from
him received a formal, oral statement in answer to our letter of
December 14th. In his reply, among other points he said that
they would station guards at the entrances to the Zone; that the

南京安全区国际委员会
宁海路5号

1937年12月17日

日本帝国大使馆，
南京。

敬请转交
日本大使馆二等秘书
福井清（Kiyoshi Fukui）先生收。

敬启者：

鉴于冈崎胜男（Katsuo Okazaki）总领事昨日下午声称国际委员会不具备法律地位，看来有必要对我方立场作些说明。对于贵国日本当局，我们并未主张任何政治地位。但是，南京市马市长于12月1日将市政府在过渡紧急状态下的几乎所有职能移交给本委员会，包括警务、重要公用事业监管、消防、住房管理、粮食供应及卫生。因此，当贵军于12月13日（星期一）中午胜利进入城市时，我们是城中唯一仍在运作的行政机构。当然，该权限仅限于安全区本身，并不涉及区内任何主权权利。

作为唯一的行政机构，并已获得上海日本当局的保证，即如果安全区内没有士兵或军事设施，贵军将不会故意攻击该区，我们试图立即与贵军先头部队建立联系。12月13日下午，我们在汉中路发现一名队长正带领一群日本士兵休息。我们向他解释了安全区的位置，并在他的地图上做了标记。我们礼貌地提请他注意三家红十字会医院，并告知了已解除武装的士兵情况。他的态度令人宽慰，因此我们觉得贵军已完全理解。

当晚及次日清晨，我们起草了12月14日的信函并将其翻译成日文。随后，正如日本帝国大使馆武官福田德三（Fukuda）先生可能告知您的那样，拉贝（Rabe）先生、史迈斯（Smythe）先生和福斯特（Forster）牧师前去寻找一位日本高级军官，以便向其递交该信函。我们与五位不同的军官进行了交谈，但他们让我们等待次日最高指挥官的到来。

翌日早晨，即12月15日，日本帝国大使馆的福田德寿（Tokuyasu Fukuda）先生光临敝处，关口（Sekiguchi）先生也携日本帝国海军“濑户”号（H.I.J.M.S. Seto）舰长及军官的名片来访。我们将上述12月14日的信函呈交给福田先生，并向关口先生保证，我们乐意合作启动电力厂的工作。中午，我们有幸在交通银行会见了天北馆长（T'ien Pei Kuan Chang，音译）负责人，并从他那里收到了对我们12月14日来函的正式口头答复。在他的回复中，除其他要点外，他表示：他们将在安全区入口处部署警卫；平民

civilian police could patrol within the Zone provided they were
armed only with batons; that the Committee could use the 10,000
tan of rice it had stored and move in the other stores of rice
assigned to it by the former City Government; and that it was
essential to repair the telephone, electricity and water works as
soon as possible. But no answer was given to point 4 in our letter
of the 14th excepting to say that people should return to their
homes as soon as possible.

On the basis of this reply, we encouraged our police to
go ahead with their duties assured the people they would be well-
treated now that we had explained to the Japanese officers, and
started to move rice. But since then any truck that appeared on
the streets without a westerner on it has been commandeered; the
Red Swastika Society (working under our direction), which started
trucks Tuesday morning to pick up dead bodies in the Zone, had its
trucks either taken or attempts made to take them, and now yesterday
14 of their workers were taken away. Our police were interfered
with and yesterday 50 of whom stationed at the Ministry of Justice
were marched off, "to be killed" according to the Japanese officer
in charge, and yesterday afternoon 46 of our "volunteer police"
were similarly marched off. (These volunteers had been organized
by our Committee on December 13th when it looked as though the work
to be done in the Zone was greater than the uniformed police - who
were on day and night duty - could take care of. These "volunteer
police" were neither uniformed nor armed in any way. They simply
wore our armbands. They were more like Boy Scouts in the West who
do odd jobs in helping to keep crowds in order, clean up, and render
first aid, etc.) On the 14th our four fire trucks were commandeered
by Japanese soldiers and used for transport.

The point we have been trying so hard to get across to
your Embassy and to the Japanese Army is that we were left to carry
on the City Government services for the civilian population of
Nanking until the Japanese authorities could establish a new City
Government or other organization to take over these functions in
the city. But unfortunately your soldiers have not been willing to
let us continue with our maintenance of order and services for the
civilian population in the Zone. This resulted in a breaking down
of our system for maintaining order and for providing necessary
services which we had carried on up till the morning of December
14th. In other words, on the 13th when your troops entered the
city, we had nearly all the civilian population gathered in a Zone
in which there had been very little destruction by stray shells and
no looting by Chinese soldiers even when in full retreat. The stage
was all set for you to take over that area peacefully and let the
normal life therein continue undisturbed until the rest of the city
could be put in order. Then the full normal life of the city could
go forward. All 27 Westerners in the city at that time and our
Chinese population were totally surprised by the reign of robbery,
rapine, and killing initiated by your soldiers on the 14th!

All that we are asking in our protests is that you restore
order amongst your troops and get the normal life of the city going
as soon as possible. In the latter process we are glad to cooperate
in any way we can. But even last night between 8 and 9 p.m. when
five Western members of our staff and Committee toured the Zone to
observe conditions, we did not find a single Japanese patrol either
in the Zone or at its entrances! Yesterday's threats and marching
off of our police had driven all our police from the streets. All
we saw were groups of 2 and 3 Japanese soldiers wandering about
the streets of the Zone and now, as I write, reports are pouring in
from all parts of the Zone about the depredations of robbery and rape
committed by these wandering, uncontrolled soldiers. This means
that nothing has been done about our requests in our letter of
yesterday, December 16th, namely, point 2, that stray soldiers be

警察可以在区内巡逻，但只能配备警棍；委员会可以使用其储存的一万担大米，并运入前市政府分配给它的其他大米储备；以及必须尽快修复电话、电力和自来水设施。但对于我们14日来函中的第4点，除称人们应尽快返回家园外，未予答复。

基于此答复，我们鼓励警察继续履行职责，向民众保证既然已向日本军官解释清楚，他们将受到良好对待，并开始运粮。但自那以后，任何出现在街道上且车上无西方人的卡车均被征用；红卍字会（在本委员会指导下工作）于周二早晨派出卡车在区内收殓尸体，其卡车要么被抢走，要么有人试图抢走，昨天其14名工人被带走。我们的警察受到干扰，昨天驻扎在司法部的50名警察被带队押走，据负责的日本军官称是“去处决”，昨天下午我们46名“志愿警察”也以同样方式被带队押走。（这些志愿者是本委员会于12月13日组织的，当时看来区内的工作量超过了身着制服的警察——他们日夜值班——所能承担的范围。这些“志愿警察”既无制服也无任何武器。他们仅佩戴我们的臂章。他们更像西方的童子军，从事维持人群秩序、清洁和提供急救等杂务。）14日，我们的四辆消防车被日本士兵征用并用于运输。

我们一直努力向贵使馆和日本军队传达的一点是：在日本当局建立新的市政府或其他组织以接管城市这些职能之前，我们被留任为南京平民人口维持市政府服务。但不幸的是，贵军士兵不愿让我们继续在区内维持秩序和为平民提供服务。这导致我们直至12月14日上午一直在运行的维持秩序和提供必要服务的体系崩溃。换言之，13日当贵军进入城市时，我们将几乎全部平民聚集在一个区内，该区几乎没有遭受流弹破坏，即使在中国军队全面撤退时也没有发生中国士兵的抢劫。一切已准备就绪，供你们和平接管该区域，让其中的正常生活不受干扰地继续，直到城市的其余部分恢复秩序。然后，城市的全面正常生活便可向前推进。当时城内的所有27名西方人和我们的中国居民完全没想到，14日贵军士兵竟开启了抢劫、掠夺和杀戮的恐怖统治！

我们在抗议中所要求的只是贵方整顿军纪，并尽快使城市的正常生活恢复运转。在后一过程中，我们乐意以任何可能的方式予以合作。但即便是在昨晚8点至9点间，当我们委员会的五位西方成员巡视全区以观察情况时，我们在区内或其入口处未发现任何日本巡逻队！昨天的威胁和押走我们警察的行为已将所有警察赶出街道。我们看到的只是三五成群的日本士兵在区内街道上闲逛，而在我写此信时，关于这些游荡、不受控制的士兵所犯下的抢劫和强奸暴行的报告正从全区各地涌来。这意味着我们昨天（12月16日）来信中的请求，即第2点，由入口处的警卫阻止散兵进入安全区，未得到任何落实。

kept out of the Zone by guards at the entrances.

Consequently, as a first step in turning over to your
authorities the maintenance of order in the Zone, we suggest :

1. That the Imperial Japanese Army set up a system of regular mili-
tary police to patrol the Zone both day and night with full
authority to arrest soldiers found looting, entering houses, and
committing rape or carrying off women.

2. That the Japanese authorities take over the 450 Chinese police
assigned to us by the former Chinese Nanking City Government
organized them to maintain peace and order amongst the civilian
population. (This order has never once broken down in the Zone).

3. In view of the number of fires in the city yesterday and last
night, fortunately not in the Zone, we suggest that the Fire
Department be re organized under your authorities and the four
trucks be returned by your soldiers to such service.

4. We further respectfully beg to suggest that as soon as possible
you kindly bring an expert in Municipal Administration to Nanking
to manage the life of the civilian population until a new city
government can be formed. (There is nothing left of the former
city government excepting the police and firemen in our Zone and
three clerks. All others left the city. The army has taken the
physical structure of the city of Nanking and the poorer sections
of its population, but most of the trained intelligentsia and active
people have all moved further west)

May we again reassure you that we have no interest in con-
tinuing any semi administrative function left to us by the former
Nanking City Government. We earnestly hope that you will kindly
take up these functions as quickly as possible. Then we will be
come simply a relief organization.

If the depredations of the last three days continue this
relief problem is going to be multiplied rapidly. We organized the
Zone on the basis that every family that could should make private
arrangements for housing and food in order to reduce the administra-
tive load suddenly placed on our ad hoc organization. But if the
present situation continues, in a few days we are going to have large
numbers of people facing starvation, their private supplies of food
and fuel are running out, money clothing and personal articles have
been taken from many of them by wandering Japanese soldiers; and
little normal business or other activity can be carried on because
people are afraid to either open shops or appear on the streets.
On the other hand, since the morning of December 14th, our supply
trucks have been practically at a standstill. Before your troops
entered the city we concentrated on getting supplies into the Zone
and expected to carry out distribution later because the people had
been urged to bring a week's supply of food with them. But in order
to keep some of our camps from going without food over a day, Western
members of our staff and committee have had to haul bags of rice to
those places in their private cars after dark!

Besides the starvation facing the people if these ser-
vices cannot be extended quickly, there is the stirring up of the
people. Some families have had their houses entered, robbed and
their women raped as much as five times in one night. Is it any
wonder that the next morning they move out and try to find a safer
place ? And yesterday afternoon while the officers of your Army
Supply Department were asking us to help get the telephone service
started, a small number of telephone workers wearing our insignia
were turned out of their houses in the Zone and are now scattered to
unknown places in the Zone. If this process of terrorism continues,

因此，作为将区内秩序维护工作移交给贵当局的第一步，我们建议：

1. 日本帝国陆军建立正规的宪兵制度，昼夜巡逻安全区，拥有充分权力逮捕被发现进行抢劫、闯入民宅、实施强奸或掳掠妇女的士兵。

2. 日本当局接管原中国南京市政府分配给我们的450名中国警察，组织他们维持平民中的和平与秩序。（该秩序在区内从未崩溃过）。

3. 鉴于昨天和昨晚城内发生火灾的数量（幸运的是不在区内），我们建议消防部门在贵当局领导下重组，并由贵军士兵归还四辆消防车以供此类服务使用。

4. 我们进一步恭敬地建议，贵方尽快派遣一位市政管理专家来南京，在新市政府成立之前管理平民生活。（原市政府除了在我们区内的警察、消防员和三名职员外，已不复存在。其他人均已离开城市。军队占据了南京城市的物理结构和其贫困阶层的人口，但大多数受过训练的知识分子和活跃人士均已向西迁移）

请允许我们再次向贵方保证，我们对继续履行原南京市政府留给我们的任何半行政职能毫无兴趣。我们恳切希望贵方能尽快接管这些职能。届时，我们将仅仅成为一个救济组织。

如果过去三天的暴行持续下去，这一救济问题将迅速倍增。我们组建安全区的基础是，每个有能力家庭都应自行安排住房和食物，以减轻突然加在我们这个临时组织身上的行政负担。但如果目前局势持续，几天内我们将面临大量人口饥饿，他们的私人食物和燃料储备即将耗尽，许多人的金钱、衣物和个人物品已被游荡的日本士兵抢走；由于人们不敢开店或出现在街道上，正常的商业或其他活动几乎无法开展。另一方面，自12月14日上午以来，我们的供应卡车几乎停滞不前。在贵军进入城市之前，我们集中精力将物资运入区内，并计划稍后进行分发，因为已敦促人们携带一周的食物储备。但为了让我们的一些营地不至于断粮超过一天，我们委员会和职员的西方成员不得不在天黑后用私家车将袋装大米运往这些地方！

page_data.en:
It will be next to impossible to prevent there to see the essential
services started. It is hard to see how starvation may be prevented
amongst many of the 200 000 Chinese civilians if order is not restored
at once amongst the Japanese soldiers in the city.

Assuming you take no action we shall be forced to take steps
to see that the civilian population is fed.

I am

Yours very truly,

John Rabe
Chairman of the Committee

除了如果这些服务不能迅速扩展，民众将面临饥饿之外，还有民众情绪被激起的问题。有些家庭在一夜之间房屋被闯入、抢劫，妇女被强奸多达五次。难怪第二天早上他们会搬离并试图寻找更安全的地方？昨天下午，正当贵军补给部军官要求我们帮助恢复电话服务时，少数佩戴我们徽章的电话工人被赶出他们在区内的住所，现在散落在区内不知名的地方。如果这种恐怖过程持续下去，
要看到基本服务启动将几乎不可能。如果不立即恢复城内日本士兵的秩序，很难看出如何防止20万中国平民中的许多人遭受饥饿。

假设贵方不采取行动，我们将被迫采取措施以确保平民人口得到供养。

此致

敬礼，

约翰·拉贝（John Rabe）
委员会主席

INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE FOR NANKING SAFETY ZONE
5 Ninghai Road
December 18 1937

The Imperial Japanese Embassy,
NANKING
For the kind attention of :
Mr. Kiyoshi Fukui
Second Secretary to the Japanese Embassy

Dear Sir:

We are very sorry to trouble you again but the sufferings
and needs of the 200 000 civilians for whom we are trying to care
make it urgent that we try to secure action from your military
authorities to stop the present disorder amongst Japanese soldiers
wandering through the Safety Zone

There is no time or space here to go into the cases that
are pouring in faster than we can type them out. But last night
Dr. Bates of our Committee went to the University of Nanking dor-
mitories to sleep in order to protect the 1,000 women that fled
there yesterday because of attacks in their homes. He found no
Gendarmerie on guard there nor at the new University Library Buil-
ding. When at 8.00 p.m. Mr Fitch and Dr. Smythe took Rev. W.P. Mills
to Ginling College to sleep in a house near the gate (as one or
more of us have been doing every night since the 14th in order to
protect the 3,000 women and children, yesterday augmented to
4,000 by the panic), we were seized roughly by a searching squad
and detained for over an hour. The officer had the two women in
charge of Ginling College, Miss Minnie Vautrin and Mrs. Chen, with
a friend, Mrs. Twinem, lined up at the gate and kept them there
in the cold and the men pushed them around roughly. The officer
insisted there were soldiers in the compound and he wanted to find
them and shoot them. Finally, he let us go home but would not let

1937年12月18日

日本帝国大使馆，
南京
敬请转交：
福井清先生
日本大使馆二等秘书

尊敬的先生：

我们非常抱歉再次打扰您，但我们试图照顾的20万平民所遭受的苦难和迫切需求，使得我们必须紧急争取贵国军事当局采取行动，制止目前日军士兵在安全区内游荡造成的混乱局面。

此处没有时间和篇幅去详述那些涌入速度超过我们打字速度的案件。但昨晚，本委员会的贝茨博士（Dr. Bates）前往金陵大学宿舍过夜，以保护昨天因家中遭袭而逃往那里的1,000名妇女。他发现那里以及新的金陵大学图书馆大楼都没有宪兵守卫。晚上8点，当费奇先生（Mr. Fitch）和史迈士博士（Dr. Smythe）送米尔斯牧师（Rev. W.P. Mills）到金陵女子文理学院，睡在靠近大门的一栋房子里时（自14日以来，我们中的一人或多人每晚都这样做，以保护3,000名妇女和儿童，昨天因恐慌人数增至4,000人），我们被一支搜查队粗暴地抓住并拘留了一个多小时。该军官让负责金陵女子文理学院的两位女士——魏特琳小姐（Miss Minnie Vautrin）和陈夫人，以及她们的朋友特威纳姆夫人（Mrs. Twinem）在大门口排成一排，让她们在寒冷中站立，男人们则粗暴地推搡她们。该军官坚持认为大院里有士兵，他要找到他们并将其枪决。最后，他让我们回家，但不允许

牧师。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

With the panic that has been created amongst the women who are
now flocking by the thousands to our American institutions for pro-
tection the men are being left more and more alone. For instance
there were 100 people in the old Language School at Siao T ao Yuan
up till December 16th. But because so many women were raped there
on the night of December 15th 400 women and children moved to
Ginling College, leaving 200 men! These public and institutional
buildings were originally listed to accommodate 35 000 people; now,
because of panic among the women this has increased to 50 000

MEMORANDUM ON THE INCIDENT AT THE MINISTRY OF JUSTICE

On the morning of December 16th, a group of Japanese soldiers
under an officer came to the Ministry of Justice and insisted on
carrying off most of the men to be shot — at least, that is what
the officer said he was going to do with them. He also marched out
all the police after seriously manhandling the Police Captain.
There were probably 100 persons that had the assignment to that station.

Two days previously, December 14th, a Japanese officer came
to the Ministry of Justice and inspected half of the group from
which they took about 100 men whom the officer claimed were soldiers
and left 100 men whom they considered to be civilians. This first
search of half of the men in the building was very carefully carried
out by a responsible officer who did not inspect that
part of the building, and he pro-
posed to come back the next day, December 15th, to inspect them and
see if he might find among them. No officer
came on the 15th to get them. But on the 16th, an officer came and
declared that they had taken all the soldiers at the time of the
first search on the 14th. Because he found some soldiers in this
group on the 16th (including the half which had not been previously
inspected), the officer declared that the police and we had put
soldiers in there since the first inspection.

The only persons we added to this body was a number of civi-
lians that had been forced out of other houses by Japanese sol-
diers, who were taken to the Ministry of Justice by Mr McCallum of
the University Hospital and Dr M S Bates of our Committee. The
fact that they found soldiers in the group on the 16th was not
because the Committee had added any soldiers to the group but
because the Japanese soldiers had failed to inspect the second half
of the group on the 15th as planned.

This whole incident on the morning of December 16th was ob-
served by Mr James McCallum of the University Hospital and by Mr.
Charles Riggs of our Committee and associate Housing Commissioner.
During the process, the officer threatened Mr Riggs with his sword
three times and finally hit him hard over the heart twice with his
fist. All Mr Riggs was trying to do was to explain to the officer
the situation described above in order to prevent civilians being
mistaken for former soldiers.

(signed) Lewis S. C. Smythe.
(Secretary International
Committee for Nanking Safety
Zone)

Nanking December 18 1937.

关于司法部事件的备忘录

12月16日上午，一群日本士兵在一位军官的带领下来到司法部，坚持要带走大部分男子去枪决——至少，那位军官说他要对他们这样做。他还严重殴打警察局长后，将所有警察押走。可能有大约100人被指派到该站点。

两天前，即12月14日，一名日本军官来到司法部，检查了其中一半的人群，从中带走了约100名该军官声称是士兵的人，留下了100名他们认为是平民的人。对这栋建筑内一半人的第一次搜查是由一名负责的军官非常仔细地进行的，他没有检查那部分建筑，并提议第二天，即12月15日回来检查他们，看看是否能从中发现什么。15日没有军官来带走他们。但在16日，一名军官到来，并宣称他们在14日第一次搜查时已经带走了所有士兵。因为他在16日在这群人中发现了一些士兵（包括之前未检查的那一半），该军官宣称警察和我们自第一次检查后把士兵安置在了那里。

我们添加到这群人中的唯一人员是一些被日本士兵从其他房屋赶出来的平民，他们由大学医院的麦卡伦先生（Mr. McCallum）和我们委员会的贝茨博士（Dr. M. S. Bates）带到司法部。16日他们在这群人中发现士兵的事实，并不是因为委员会向这群人添加了任何士兵，而是因为日本士兵未能按计划于15日检查这群人的另一半。

12月16日上午的整个事件由大学医院的詹姆斯·麦卡伦先生（Mr. James McCallum）和我们委员会成员兼助理住房专员查尔斯·里格斯先生（Mr. Charles Riggs）目睹。在此过程中，该军官三次用剑威胁里格斯先生，最后用拳头重重地击打他的心脏部位两次。里格斯先生所做的一切只是向该军官解释上述情况，以防止平民被误认为是前士兵。

（签名）刘易斯·S·C·史迈士（Lewis S. C. Smythe）。
（南京安全区国际委员会
秘书）

ALTERNATE OF REGISTRATION OF
REFUGEES AT THE UNIVERSITY
28 December 1937

Registration was begun in the main compound, occupied mainly by women. To the relatively small number of men there the authorities added more than 2000 from the new Library. Out of the total of about 3000 men massed together on the tennis courts below Swayzee Hall, between two and three hundred stepped out in answer to a half-hour of haranguing to this effect: "All who have been soldiers or have performed compulsory labor (fu ruh 服役) pass to the rear. Your lives will be spared, and you will be given work if you thus voluntarily come forth. If you do not, and upon inspection you are discovered, you will be shot." Short speeches were repeated many times over by Chinese under the instructions of Japanese officers. They were Chinese who wished to save as many of their people as possible from the fate that others had met as former soldiers or as men wrongfully of being former soldiers. The speeches were clearly and thoroughly heard by Mr. H.J. Sone, Mr Charles S. Riggs, and myself as well as by many Chinese members of the University staff. It was thought by some Chinese that certain men who stepped out were influenced by fear or by misunderstanding of the term for compulsory labor. Assuredly a fair number of them had never been soldiers.

The actual conduct of the registration was in the hands of officers whom we later came to know as relatively considerate and reasonable, though that is no praise nor exemption from responsibility for gross evils among their men in open daylight and in public view, even during the process of registration while the officers were present. At the outset that morning, the chief officer asked my permission for conducting the registration on American property, a deference most startling in the experience of Japanese occupation. Moreover, he and others took especial pains to avoid unnecessary fear at the beginning, and I am inclined to credit them with sincerity despite the terrible outcome. Again, although the soldiers sorted out for examination nearly one thousand from the remaining men, the officers permitted all but one of these thousand to be released for registration upon the casual "guarantees" given by various Chinese as the line was marched by for individual inspection; and that one was let go upon the joint representations of Mr Sone and myself. Furthermore, officers before noon asked that we provide two meals of rice for each of the two to three hundred "volunteers", to be replaced by rice from military stores. Even the common soldiers acting as guards were fairly kind and gave out more cigarettes than blows. In the afternoon the men reported individually their names and occupations which were written down.

Meanwhile another element had been introduced. Two additional officers, with higher status at least for this particular job, came in for inspection. One of them was violent in his dissatisfaction with what had been done. This man had shown gross roughness and stupidity during a visit to the University on the previous day, and we were often to encounter his evil doings and coarse methods as head of the military police for this district. Toward five o'clock in the afternoon, the two or three hundred men were taken away in two groups by military police. One of them in retrospect declared that he was made anxious by the unusual courtesy of some of the friendly guards.

大学难民登记之变通办法
1937年12月28日

登记工作主要在主要院落开始，那里主要居住着妇女。当局从新图书馆增加了两千多名男子，加入那里相对较少的男性人群中。在斯威齐堂（Swayzee Hall）下方网球场上聚集的大约三千名男子中，有两三百人站了出来，以回应长达半小时的如下训话：“所有当过兵或服过劳役（服役）的人退到后面。如果你们自愿站出来，将饶恕你们的性命，并给你们工作。如果不这样做，而在检查中被发现，将被枪决。”这些简短的讲话由中国人按照日本军官的指令反复宣讲。这些中国人希望尽可能多地使他们的同胞免遭其他人作为前士兵或被误认为前士兵所遭遇的命运。索恩（H.J. Sone）先生、查尔斯·S·里格斯（Charles S. Riggs）先生以及我本人，还有许多大学职员中的中国成员，都清楚而完整地听到了这些讲话。有些中国人认为，某些站出来的人是受到恐惧的影响，或是对“劳役”一词产生了误解。可以肯定的是，他们中有相当一部分人从未当过兵。

实际的登记工作由一些官员负责，我们后来了解到他们相对体贴和讲理，尽管这并不能为他们手下士兵在光天化日之下、众目睽睽之中犯下的严重暴行提供赞誉或免除责任，即便是在官员在场的登记过程中也是如此。那天早上伊始，首席军官请求我允许在美国财产上进行登记，这种恭敬态度在日本占领期间的经历中最为令人震惊。此外，他和其他人特别小心，以避免在开始时引起不必要的恐慌，尽管结果可怕，但我倾向于相信他们的诚意。再者，虽然从剩余人员中筛选出近一千名士兵进行检查，但官员们允许这一千人中除一人外的所有人，凭借各种中国人在列队接受个别检查时随意提供的“担保”，获准进行登记；而那唯一的一人，也是在索恩先生和我本人的共同交涉下被释放的。此外，中午之前，军官们要求我们为这两三百名“志愿者”每人提供两餐米饭，随后将由军用仓库的米粮替换。即使是担任警卫的普通士兵也相当友善，递出的香烟多于挥出的拳头。下午，这些人逐一报出姓名和职业，并被记录下来。

与此同时，出现了另一个因素。另外两名军官进来进行检查，至少在这项特定工作中，他们的地位较高。其中一人对已完成的工作表示强烈不满。此人在前一天访问大学时表现出极度的粗暴和愚蠢，我们后来经常遇到他作为该区宪兵队长的恶行和粗野手段。下午五点左右，这两三百人被宪兵分成两组带走。其中一人事后宣称，一些友好警卫不同寻常的礼貌使他感到焦虑。

Next morning there came to the University Hospital a man
with five bayonet wounds. On two occasions this man reported with
fair accuracy and clarity that he had been a refugee in the Library
but was not present at the tennis courts; he was picked up on the
street and added to a group that did come from the courts. That
evening somewhere to the west about 130 Japanese soldiers killed
most of 500 similar captives with bayonet thrusts. The victim re-
covered himself to find the Japanese gone, and managed to crawl back
during the night. He was not familiar with this part of Nanking
and was vague as to places. Also on the morning of the 27th there
was brought to me a man who said that he was one of 30-40 who had
escaped the death met by most of the 200-300 taken away the previous
evening. Since the man desired help for himself and one or more
companions in the registration then continuing, and since I was
surrounded by military police at the time, I had to tell him that
registration was that day limited to women, and that it was best not
to speak further at the moment. Three times later I inquired for
this group but got no response.

In the course of the same day and the next (27th and 28th) I
heard and checked circumstantial reports that part of the men taken
away had been bound in groups of five and ten, to be passed suc-
cessively from a first room of a large house into a second room or
court where there was a big fire. As each group went forward groans
and cries could be heard by the remainder but no shots. Some
twenty remaining from an original sixty broke in desperation through
a back wall and made their escape. Part of the detachment brought
from the University were said to have been saved by the pleas of
priest living in the neighborhood (Wu T'ai Shan clearly specified
in all this group of indirect reports which came in part from Budd-
hists). A similar story had been heard by Mr Riggs early in the
evening of the 26th conjecturally too soon to come from the same
incident. This confusion or complexity of reports was discouraging
and several attempts at further inquiry met with little result
while other duties and problems pressed upon each day.

On the 31st two men gave a request for aid with their story
to a trusted assistant of the Library refugee camp who offered to
bring them to me for confirmation if desired. One frankly declared
that he had been a soldier, thus creating a special presumption in
favor of his truthfulness. They said that the 200-300 men from the
University were split up into various groups. They themselves were
taken first to Wu T'ai Shan then to the bank of the canal outside
Han Hsi Men where a machine gun was turned upon them. They fell,
one of them wounded among the dead men and smeared with their blood.

On the 3rd of January, an interview was secured with two men
among five acquaintances in the Library, who were survivors of
the experience of 26 December. One of them was in the first group
taken from the University, and confirmed substantially the room-
and-fire account at Wu T'ai Shan as given above under the date of
the 27th and 28th. He estimated that of his group 80 were killed
and 40-50 escaped. One of them, wounded by a bayonet thrust, was
in the Library, and could be brought to report the same facts.

The second was an unusually intelligent man, clear and specific
both in narrative and under cross-questioning. He was taken with
the second group to a large house at Wu T'ai Shan opposite a temple
(this site has been identified with considerable assurance as one of
two buildings on Shanghai Road or an alley from it, across from the

第二天早上，一名身中五处刺刀伤的男子来到大学医院。此人两次相当准确和清晰地报告说，他曾是图书馆的难民，但当时并不在网球场；他是在街上被抓走的，并被加入了一群确实来自网球场的人中。那天晚上，在西部某地，约130名日本士兵用刺刀刺杀了500名类似俘虏中的大多数人。受害者苏醒后发现日本人已离开，并在夜间设法爬回。他不熟悉南京的这一部分，对地点的描述模糊不清。同样在27日早上，有人向我带来一名男子，他说自己是30-40名幸存者之一，逃脱了前一晚被带走的200-300人中大多数人所遭遇的死亡命运。由于该男子希望为自己和一名或多名同伴寻求帮助，以便参加当时正在进行的登记，而且我当时被宪兵包围，我不得不告诉他，当天的登记仅限于妇女，此刻最好不要再多说。后来我曾三次询问这群人的情况，但未得到回应。

在同一天及次日（27日和28日）的过程中，我听到并核实了一些细节丰富的报告，称部分被带走的男子被五人或十人一组捆绑起来，依次从一所大房子的第一个房间进入第二个房间或庭院，那里有一堆大火。当每组人向前移动时，剩下的人能听到呻吟和哭喊声，但没有枪声。原本六十人中约有二十人在绝望中冲破后墙逃脱。据说，从大学带来的分遣队中的一部分人，因居住在附近的牧师（在所有这些部分来自佛教徒的间接报告中，明确指定为五台山）的求情而得救。里格斯先生在26日晚些时候也听到过类似的故事，但推测时间过早，不可能来自同一事件。这种报告的混乱或复杂性令人沮丧，几次进一步查询的尝试收效甚微，而其他职责和问题每天都紧迫地压在身上。

31日，两名男子向图书馆难民营的一位可信助手提出援助请求，并讲述了他们的故事，该助手表示如果需要，愿意带他们来找我确认。其中一人坦承自己曾是一名士兵，从而为其真实性提供了特殊的有利推定。他们说，来自大学的200-300名男子被分成各个小组。他们自己先被带到五台山，然后被带到汉西门外的运河岸边，在那里机枪向他们扫射。他们倒下了，其中一人受伤倒在死人堆中，身上沾满了鲜血。

1月3日，我在图书馆的五名熟人中安排了两名男子进行面谈，他们是12月26日经历的幸存者。其中一人属于从大学带走的第一组人，并大体证实了上述27日和28日日期下关于五台山房间和火灾的说法。他估计他的组中有80人被杀，40-50人逃脱。其中一人被刺刀刺伤，目前在图书馆，可以带来报告相同的事实。

第二人是一位异常聪明的人，在叙述和接受盘问时都清晰具体。他与第二组人一起被带到五台山的一座大房子，对面是一座寺庙（该地点已被相当确定地认定为上海路或其附近小巷上的两座建筑之一，位于北边不远处的美国学校对面）。

he was alarmed by noticing Chinese priests and a Japanese priest
sorrowfully praying and putting long strips of paper at the entrance
to the temple. (Since the report of a Japanese priest in Nanking
was an utter novelty I sceptically asked how he knew that the priest
was Japanese. The informant replied that his footwear was cleft
for a separate big toe; and later I learned that the informant had
lived in Tientsin where he would naturally acquire such recognition.
A few days later I myself saw such a priest on Shanghai Road).
Sensing that the atmosphere was ominous, the man spoke to a guard
who had been friendly indicating his anxiety. The guard silently
wrote in the dirt with a stick ta ien ming ling "orders
from the big fellow" The men in the immediate vicinity of my in-
formant (he did not speak of others) were bound with wire wrist to
wrist, in pairs. Thirty or more were taken to Han Chung Men and
across the canal where four or five in desperation broke from the
column in the dusk or dark taking advantage of protecting walls and
found a hiding-place. The man guessed by the moon that it was about
one o'clock when he heard despairing cries not far to the north.
At daybreak he went a little in that direction and saw bodies in
rows, bayoneted. Though in great fear he managed to get past the
gate safely and slip back to the Safety Zone.

To the account of this man and his testimony must be added two
items. A responsible worker in the Chinese Red Cross requested us
to go outside of Han Chung Men to inspect a large number of bodies
there. Mr. Kröger of the International Committee told me that he
observed these bodies himself in the course of an early venture
outside the gate, but that they could not be seen from the City Wall.
The gate is now closed. The original informant talked so freely
to me because he had a premonition of trouble during registration
which he was about to attempt. On January 7, I believe he was one
of some ten men sorted out by the military police from the men pass-
ing before them in the open registration resumed on the University
compound. During that week the officers who did the actual work
seemed to be under instructions to get about that many men per day,
or perhaps to feel that they could satisfy their superiors with no-
thing less. (Naturally the voluntary admission of previous mili-
tary service had practically ceased, and the whole procedure of re-
gistration had changed greatly from the earlier times). As usual,
I tried to watch these performances with some closeness and to give
a little help so far as the personnel and temper of the military
would permit in each shifting hour. Failing in indirect efforts
after I had observed that this man was among the ten I searched for
a chance and took the best of the officers there with me claiming
(with some stretch for which I hope to be forgiven!) that I recog-
nized the man and one other who looked most promising among the re-
mainder and should like the favour of guaranteeing them. The se-
cond was released, but not my acquaintance, for reasons unfathomable;
and further efforts brought such a kick-back that I had to desist for
fear of injury to others. Death was the probable outcome, though
not certainly so.

Two other men from the University Library reported indirectly
that they escaped from a large body of several hundred who were
bayoneted along the canal well to the north, near to San Chah Ho.

Finally, it should be remembered that this whole incident is
only one of a series that had been going on for two weeks, with
changes on the main theme of mass murder of men accused rightfully
or wrongfully of being ex-soldiers. This is not the place to dis-
cuss the dictum of international law that the lives of prisoners are

对此人的叙述和证词，还需补充两点。中国红十字会的一名负责人请求我们去汉中门外 inspect 大量尸体。国际委员会的克罗格（Kröger）先生告诉我，他在早期冒险出门时亲自观察到了这些尸体，但从城墙上无法看到。现在城门已关闭。最初的 informant 之所以如此自由地向我讲述，是因为他对即将尝试参加的登记怀有不祥的预感。我相信，在1月7日，他是大约十名男子中的一员，这些男子是在大学院落恢复公开登记时，从经过宪兵面前的人群中被筛选出来的。在那一周里，实际执行工作的军官似乎接到指示，每天要抓获大约这么多的人，或者也许觉得只有这样才能让上级满意。（当然，自愿承认先前兵役的情况实际上已经停止，整个登记程序与早期相比发生了巨大变化）。像往常一样，我试图密切观察这些行动，并在军事人员及其情绪允许的范围内，在每个变化的时刻提供一点帮助。在观察到这名男子在那十人之中后，间接努力失败，我寻找机会，带上那里最好的军官，声称（带着一些我希望能被原谅的夸张！）我认出了这名男子，以及在其余人员中看起来最有希望的另一人，并希望得到担保他们的优待。第二人被释放，但我的熟人却没有，原因深不可测；进一步的努力遭到了强烈的抵制，我不得不罢手，以免伤害其他人。死亡可能是结果，虽然并非绝对确定。

另外两名来自大学图书馆的男子间接报告说，他们从数百人的大群体中逃脱，该群体在更北部的三汊河附近的运河沿岸被刺刀刺杀。

最后，应当记住，整个事件只是持续两周的一系列事件中的一起，其主题始终是对被正确或错误指控为前士兵的男子进行大规模屠杀。此处不宜讨论国际法中关于战俘生命应受保护的准则……

除非出于严重的军事需要，否则应予保留；日本人也不应为了对据称在战斗中杀害了目前占领南京的部队战友的人进行明目张胆的报复而置该法律于不顾。其他事件涉及的人数比这一事件更多。我对这些情况的特别关注有两方面：第一，因为迫使人们自投罗网走向死亡的条款极其背信弃义；第二，因为我们的财产、人员以及受我们保护者（难民）与这起巨大罪行的各个阶段有着令人痛心的密切关联。此外，关于谋杀的方法、地点和时间的总体证据，比某些其他案件更为充分，在那些案件中，大批人被带走后一去不返，但我们只掌握零星的信息。作为一个总体结论，似乎很清楚，从大学带走的绝大多数人都在当晚被杀害，其中一些人是与其他来源的人群混在一起后被杀的。

即使在这几周的残酷麻木中，经过那些网球场仍然令人难以忍受。几天来不得不应付在这场闹剧中扮演不同角色的军官和士兵，为了成千上万被带到大学登记的人的福祉，必要时还得对他们强颜欢笑、毕恭毕敬，这简直是一种折磨。人们感到，他和他的基督教机构已成为杀害两百人的帮凶，如果能在周围这片苦难的海洋中找到那些可怜的受赡养者，就要对他们的命运负责。与我们所面对的那些暴力团伙相比，部分军官和士兵还算人道，他们中许多人一定有妻儿，他们对家人是仁慈的

Japanese troops in Nanking In explanation he pointed out the long

Russo-Jap war and Man-
churian incident, which had been near home there were no atrocities

2月5日，外国代表受邀会见南京卫戍司令松井少将。将军发表了一项声明，其要点如下：

为日军在南京犯下的暴行进行了辩解。他解释说，这是因为其部队经历了长期而激烈的战斗，以及中国人的顽强抵抗。快速推进、粮食供应普遍失败以及部队疲惫不堪，导致纪律涣散，从而发生了抢劫和暴力行为。日俄战争和满洲事变后，由于战事靠近本土，南京并未发生暴行，外国人会克制批评，不会像对待日本民族那样严厉。目前正在努力恢复纪律。日军对此不应受到指责，尽管他们对蒋介石试图在中国民众及军队中灌输的反日情绪感到愤怒。日本军方当局希望恢复城内的正常生活。在扬州，日军与中国人之间的关系良好，但在南京，外国人的干涉阻碍了恢复正常秩序，大量中国人继续居住在所谓的安全区内。他特别提到了“某国”（即美国）的报告和活动，这些损害了日本与该国的关系。他不喜欢外国人采取的那种如同法庭法官般的态度，并警告他们，他们的批评以及在日本人和中国人之间的干涉会激怒日军，可能导致一些不愉快的事件。他请求得到信任，并保证将尽力在短时间内恢复法律和秩序以及正常的城市生活，以便外国家庭可以返回南京。他将尽力保护外国人的权利和财产，并请外国代表与他讨论困难，但不要干涉涉及日本人和中国人的事务。

NOTES ON PRESENT SITUATION

Tuesday noon
February 8th, 1938

LATEST MURDER MYSTERY SOLVED

The old, gray-haired Chinese who was shot at the edge of a garden patch near the city wall back of Pei Tze Ting was shot by Japanese soldiers for carrying two chairs from a matshed. The old women and two men who came with an old door to carry away the wounded man were shot for their humanitarian interest in helping the wounded man.

The latest demonstration of the serious endeavor to restore law and order in Nanking occurred late Sunday afternoon. Because the first report to us Monday morning said it was in a military area we did not go then to investigate. But later in the day a neighbor of the deceased came and then about 4:30 p.m. a girl came and said she was the daughter of the woman who had been killed. Her mother had gone home a few days ago to start their home again and took all their money with her. She hoped to find the money on her mother's body. Mr. Rabe and Mr. Mills went with her to the scene immediately and found the four bodies located thus with fresh pools of blood:

Case No. 425. Number 1 is the old man who was shot first; number 2 is the woman who brought aid; numbers 3 and 4 are the men who came to get the wounded man; the oblong object is the door.
〔此处有一幅手绘现场示意图，标注有 POND, wire fence, shrine 等字样及数字编号〕

This morning, Tuesday, Herr Dr. Rosen, Mr. Rabe, Mr. Sperling, and Mr. Smythe went to investigate and found the bodies had been moved to a nearby knoll for burial but the blood was still on the ground and on the door. The scene of the murder is near a pond surrounded by garden patches, two of which were freshly dug up for spring planting. It is 200 yards from the nearest road. This morning soldiers were passing on the road but no sentries were found in front of the matshed houses of the farmers. The one man left told us there were many people who had returned that were working their ground on the day of the killing. But this frightened them all away. Thus is agricultural production encouraged! To the west the charred walls of the former Soviet Embassy rise skyward.

FOOD. The trucking department of the Self-Government Committee is trucking in 1,500 bags of flour a day and getting started on the 1,000 bags of rice recently assigned. Flour can now be purchased on Pac Tai Chieh just beyond Shih Miao K'o.

RETURN OF REFUGEES TO THEIR HOMES. The figure announced today in Shanghai that 100,000 refugees had returned to their homes may be a little high as that does not allow for those that return to the Zone. About one-third have moved out of the camps, i.e., 30,000. A Westerner who was out South Gate this morning reports more people out there and not so much burning farther away from the gate.

General Matsui's instructions to the officers yesterday that order must be restored is most welcome. Then we can stop the bother of reporting.

407. Feb. 5th, 7.30 p.m. five Japanese soldiers came to the home of Mai Liang Shih on Tien Chao Lu and searched many men for money and attempted to rape Mrs. Mai but she escaped.

408
page_data.zh:
当前局势笔记

星期二中午
1938年2月8日

最新谋杀谜案已解

那位在北极亭后方城墙附近的一块菜园边缘被枪杀的中国白发老人，是因为从草棚里搬两把椅子而被日本士兵枪杀的。带着旧门板来抬走伤者的老妇人和两名男子，也因出于人道主义兴趣帮助伤者而被枪杀。

最近一次展示在南京恢复法律和秩序的严肃努力发生在周日下午晚些时候。因为周一早上给我们的第一份报告说事发地在军事区域，所以我们当时没有去调查。但当天晚些时候，死者的一位邻居来了，随后在下午4:30左右，一个女孩来了，说她是被杀妇女的女儿。她母亲几天前回家重新安家，带走了所有的钱。她希望在母亲的尸体上找到这笔钱。拉贝先生和米尔斯先生立即随她前往现场，发现四具尸体位于此处，周围有新鲜的血泊：

案件编号425。1号是最先被枪杀的老人；2号是前来援助的妇女；3号和4号是来抬走伤者的男子；长方形物体是门板。
〔此处有一幅手绘现场示意图，标注有 POND, wire fence, shrine 等字样及数字编号〕

今天早上，星期二，罗森博士、拉贝先生、施佩林先生和史迈斯先生前去调查，发现尸体已被移至附近的小山丘埋葬，但地面上和门板上仍有血迹。谋杀现场靠近一个被菜园环绕的池塘，其中两块菜地刚为春耕翻过土。现场距离最近的道路有200码。今天早上有士兵在路上经过，但在农民的草棚房前未发现哨兵。留下的一名男子告诉我们，杀戮当天有许多回来耕种土地的人。但这把他们都吓跑了。农业生产力就是这样得到鼓励的！向西望去，前苏联大使馆的焦黑墙壁高耸入云。

食品。自治委员会的卡车部门每天运进1500袋面粉，并开始运送最近分配的1000袋大米。现在可以在石庙口以外的太平街购买面粉。

难民返回家园。今天上海宣布有10万难民返回家园，这一数字可能略高，因为这未计入返回安全区的人。约有三分之一的人已搬出难民营，即3万人。一位今天早上在南门外的西方人报告说，那里的人多了，离城门较远的地方焚烧情况也不那么严重了。

松井将军昨天向军官下达必须恢复秩序的命令，这是最受欢迎的消息。这样我们就可以停止报告的麻烦了。

407. 2月5日，晚上7:30，五名日本士兵来到朝天路麦梁氏（音译）家中，搜查多名男子的钱财，并企图强奸麦太太，但她逃脱了。

408

page_data.en:
- 2 -

408. Feb.5th, 7.40 p.m. two Japanese soldiers came to the home of Chi Chi Shih on I Ho Road, took $ 5.00 and attempted to rape the women but they escaped.

409. Feb.5th, 8 a.m., two Japanese soldiers came to the home of Er Li Shih, who had gone home on Feb.3rd, at Kuang Yuan Chieh near Confucian Temple. At the time the men of the wine shop were away doing work for the Japanese. They dragged her into a room and closed the door for over ten minutes. She was forced to take off her clothes. She had given birth to a child ten days ago, but the child had died. Another woman at the same place, Feng Ho Shih, saved herself from violence at the same time by lying that she had given birth to a child four days before but the child was dead. The soldiers promised to come back later to examine her.

410. Feb.5th, 10 a.m. 4 or 5 Japanese soldiers came into the home of Wang Liu Shih at Wang Ni Kang asking for girls and children. At 5 p.m. there came again some other soldiers knocking the door vigorously. Wang Lu Shih and family fled through the back door. They had returned home on Feb. 4th according to order.

411. Feb. 4th, Miss Vautrin reports that 8 men for working 7 or 8 days were given a hundred German mark note dated "7 February 1908", (Of course the note is worthless) as remuneration.
(Vautrin) (The note is on file).

412. Feb.4th, at 4 p.m. Three soldiers (two armed ones) came to a house on Hua Hsing Hsiang (east of Ninghai Road) and searched for money and demanded girls. The old women were so frightened that they ran away. The soldiers failed to get them.

413. Feb.4th, afternoon, a woman named Feng went back home (Pao Ma Hsiang) but when she arrived at Fu Ming Fang, she was dragged by two Japanese soldiers into a dugout. They tried to do violence, but owing to the cry of her child they went away.

414. Feb.3rd, morning, Wu's whole family returned home to Lung Pei Li. A Japanese soldier entered the house twice and took away nearly all the articles. The same soldier entered again and drove away all the males. He tore the clothes off a woman (the 6th na na, married woman) and raped her by force.

415. Feb.3rd, about 5 p.m. at Chang Su Hsiang (near Ta Chung Chiao) three soldiers came and forced a woman to throw away her baby and after raping her they went away laughing.

416. Hsung Tsoh Shih reports that when she went out of the Safety Zone, as she reached Hsuisimen she was searched by soldiers stationed at the gate and $ 3.80 was taken from her. When she went out of the gate, she was dragged into a dugout. She was saved from violence when the soldier saw a younger woman about 30 years of age and let her go and caught the younger woman. Hsung Tsoh Shih fled back into the city.

417. Feb.4, at Man Hsi, Tai Ping Chiao, three Japanese soldiers came to Tu's home and wanted to rape the woman. When she heard the voice of the soldiers, she hid herself behind the loom. The soldiers tried to force her for 30 minutes and went away. This Tu woman came to the camp and made this report.

418
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

408. 2月5日，晚上7:40，两名日本士兵来到颐和路季季氏（音译）家中，拿走5.00美元，并企图强奸妇女，但她们逃脱了。

409. 2月5日，上午8点，两名日本士兵来到孔庙附近广源街的二李氏（音译）家中，她已于2月3日回家。当时酒铺的男人们正外出为日本人做工。他们将她拖进一个房间，关上门超过十分钟。她被迫脱掉衣服。她十天前刚生下一个孩子，但孩子已夭折。同一地方的另一名妇女冯何氏（音译），谎称自己四天前生过孩子但已死，从而在同一时间避免了暴力侵害。士兵们答应稍后回来检查她。

410. 2月5日，上午10点，4或5名日本士兵进入王泥岗王刘氏（音译）家中，索要女孩和儿童。下午5点，又有其他士兵猛烈敲门。王卢氏（音译）及其家人从后门逃走。他们是根据命令于2月4日回家的。

411. 2月4日，沃特林小姐报告说，8名工作了7或8天的工人得到了一张日期为“1908年2月7日”的一百德国马克纸币作为报酬。（当然，这张纸币毫无价值）
（沃特林）（该纸币已存档）。

412. 2月4日，下午4点。三名士兵（其中两人持枪）来到华兴巷（宁海路以东）的一处住宅，搜刮钱财并索要女孩。老妇人们吓得逃跑了。士兵们未能抓到她们。

413. 2月4日，下午，一名姓冯的妇女回家（宝马巷），但当她到达福明坊时，被两名日本士兵拖进一个防空洞/掩体。他们试图施暴，但因孩子的哭喊声而离开。

414. 2月3日，上午，吴家全家回到龙背里家中。一名日本士兵两次进入屋内，拿走了几乎所有物品。同一名士兵再次进入，驱赶所有男性。他撕下一名妇女（第六奶妈，已婚妇女）的衣服，并强行强奸了她。

415. 2月3日，下午5点左右，在张苏巷（近大中桥），三名士兵前来，强迫一名妇女扔掉婴儿，强奸她后笑着离开。

416. 熊左氏（音译）报告说，当她走出安全区，到达水西门时，被驻守城门的士兵搜身，抢走3.80美元。当她走出城门时，被拖进一个防空洞/掩体。当士兵看到一名约30岁的年轻妇女时，放过了她而去抓那名年轻妇女，她 thus 免于暴力侵害。熊左氏逃回城内。

417. 2月4日，在曼西（音译）太平桥，三名日本士兵来到杜家，企图强奸该妇女。听到士兵的声音后，她躲在织布机后面。士兵们试图强迫她达30分钟，随后离开。这位杜姓妇女来到难民营作了此报告。

418

page_data.en:
- 3 -

418. Feb. 3rd, four Japanese soldiers climbed over the wall of a
house on Peiping Road at 8.00 p.m. and took away $ 1.00 from
Mr. Sih, $ 3.00 from Mr. Tao and raped the wife of Mr. Chao
and the wife of Mr. Liu twice.

419. Feb. 3rd, three Japanese soldiers went to another house on
Peiping Road at about 8.00 p.m. and took $ 2.20 from Mr. King,
$ 2.50 from Mr. Hu and $ 1.40 from Mr. Too.

420. Feb. 3rd, Yao Lao Shih who had returned home aged 23, was
raped by Japanese soldiers at 1.00 p.m

421. Feb. 2nd, Wang Yu Ling took his wife to go home this morning,
but when they were on the midway they met a truck which was
loaded with three Japanese soldiers passing by and the truck
was suddenly stopped. The soldiers came down and took the
said refugee's box to the truck and also his wife. Fortunately
his wife jumped down from the truck but his box was taken
away.

422. Feb. 2nd, Wang Yang Shih went to her home, which is situated at
Pan Lung San outside Ho Ping Gate. At 11.00 a.m. the same
morning four Japanese soldiers came and intended to rape.
After begging them ardently by kneeling down, they set the
women free but beat them hardly and took away ten dollars.
Fearing that they would come back again, Mr. Wang and her
children returned to the camp.

423. Feb. 2nd, Hse Chen Shih, aged 24, on her way home to Hsiakwan
was detained in a house by Japanese soldiers and violated.
When she went out the gate to Hsiakwan, she was dragged by 3
or 4 Japanese soldiers. Fortunately, she was saved by Japanese
Navy officer. Through the aid of Swastika people she was
brought back to the refugee camp.

424. Feb. 1st, six refugees went home from one camp to Si K'u Sze
Fang at noon. One soldier came and after looking around went
and brought another soldier. They threatened the refugees
with bayonets and robbed them of $ 8.30 and 12 dimes.

(sd.) L. Smythe.

(incomplete).
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

418. 2月3日，晚上8时，四名日本士兵翻越北平路一处房屋的围墙，从施先生处抢走1.00美元，从陶先生处抢走3.00美元，并两次强奸了赵先生的妻子和刘先生的妻子。

419. 2月3日，晚上8时许，三名日本士兵前往北平路的另一处房屋，从金先生处抢走2.20美元，从胡先生处抢走2.50美元，从杜先生（音译）处抢走1.40美元。

420. 2月3日，下午1时，23岁的姚女士（音译）在回家途中被日本士兵强奸。

421. 2月2日，王玉林（音译）今晨携妻回家，但在半途中遇到一辆载有三名日本士兵的卡车驶过，卡车突然停下。士兵下车，将该难民的箱子搬上卡车，并将其妻子也带上车。幸而其妻子从卡车上跳下逃脱，但箱子被抢走。

422. 2月2日，王女士（音译）前往位于和平门外蟠龙三（音译）的家中。当日上午11时，四名日本士兵前来意图强奸。经跪地苦苦哀求后，他们放过了这些妇女，但对其严加殴打，并抢走十元。因担心士兵再次返回，王先生及其子女返回了难民收容所。

423. 2月2日，24岁的谢女士（音译）在回下关（Hsiakwan）家中的途中，被日本士兵扣留在屋内并遭侵犯。当她走出前往下关的大门时，被三四名日本士兵拖拽。幸而一名日本海军军官将其救下。通过卐字会（Swastika people）的协助，她被带回难民收容所。

424. 2月1日，中午时分，六名难民从某收容所回家前往四库寺坊（Si K'u Sze Fang，音译）。一名士兵到来，四处张望后离开并带来了另一名士兵。他们用刺刀威胁难民，抢走8.30美元及12角。

（签名）L. Smyth。

（不完整）。
